record.field: Get the next Odoo version counterpart of a code element (model, field, method or data record): where did it go? Move-aware (renames, replacements, cross-module and cross-model moves), following the confirmed module timelines (renames/replacements), the confirmed code timelines and the model's next version record. A draft proposal already declared for the element is reported in 'proposal' without changing 'found', 'state' or 'next', which follow confirmed timelines only.

Get the version chain of a code element: its successive names, modules, models and Odoo versions, from the oldest to the newest known version, with the timeline (move/replacement/removal) linking each step to the next one.

List the code element moves/replacements/removals declared in the database, with their review state: draft timelines are proposals pending review, not applied to the analysis yet. Results can be filtered by state, element type and timeline type, and are paginated.

List the code elements of a module that are absent from its next Odoo version: the inventory feeding the migration analysis. For each element the timeline already covering it is reported with a 'resolution' status (uncovered = to analyze and propose, draft = proposal in progress, removed = confirmed removal), together with counters before pagination. Elements whose next version is not scanned yet are excluded. Data elements expose their data_type, noupdate and is_override flags and can be filtered on them, so demo, noupdate and overriding records can be told apart from structural records; only data records loaded by the module are listed. Model elements expose the modules still defining the same model in the next version ('next_defined_in').

Declare that a code element (model, field, method or data record) has been renamed, replaced, moved to another module/model or removed, starting from the next Odoo version. Use 'next_module' and/or 'next_model' for a cross-module or cross-model move; 'next_name' can be omitted when the element keeps its name/XML ID. Prefer a 'moved' timeline with the target over a 'removed' one when the target is known: it preserves the link for the migration analysis. The 'note' is HTML: start with the confidence tag, then end with a bulleted Source section, one full URL per link (commit first); do not use Markdown. The proposal is created as a draft timeline by default; set 'confirm' to true to create it directly as confirmed (high-confidence proposals only: it immediately impacts the migration analysis). The 'note' should document the sources of truth justifying it (e.g. the GitHub commit URL, the OpenUpgrade migration script URL): a source of truth URL is mandatory to confirm.

Update a draft code timeline proposal (type, target module/model, new element name or note). Use 'next_module' and/or 'next_model' to change the target scope of a cross-module or cross-model move; 'next_name' can be omitted to keep the current target name/XML ID. The 'note' is HTML: start with the confidence tag, then end with a bulleted Source section, one full URL per link (commit first); do not use Markdown. Prefer a 'moved' timeline with the target over a 'removed' one when the target is known. Set 'confirm' to true to confirm it once the proposal reaches high confidence (a confirmed timeline immediately impacts the migration analysis, and a source of truth URL is required in 'note'). A confirmed timeline can only have its note updated, and the new note must carry a source URL; semantic fields cannot be modified.
Delete a draft code timeline proposal. Confirmed timelines cannot be deleted: they are managed by humans in the UI.
